Operating Systems for AI Engineers

Chapter 02 of 322 · Core Computer Science for AI Engineers

Operating systems manage hardware resources and provide abstractions for process management, memory, and I/O. Understanding OS concepts is crucial for optimizing AI workloads and managing GPU resources.

slides.label: MODULE 00 · Core Computer Science for AI Engineers
slides.title: Operating Systems for AI Engineers

slides.label: KEY IDEA 01
slides.title: Process vs Thread
slides.body: A process is an independent execution unit with its own address space, file descriptors, and system state. A thread is a lighter unit within a process — threads share the address space but have their own stack and registers.

slides.label: KEY IDEA 02
slides.title: Scheduling
slides.body: The Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS) in Linux gives each runnable thread a proportion of CPU time. It uses a red-black tree of tasks sorted by vruntime (virtual runtime). Lower nice values = higher priority = less vruntime growth.

slides.label: KEY IDEA 03
slides.title: Memory Management
slides.body: Virtual memory provides each process with a contiguous address space mapped to physical memory through page tables. The Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) caches recent translations. A TLB miss walks the page table in hardware or software.

slides.label: KEY IDEA 04
slides.title: File Systems
slides.body: - inode: metadata structure storing permissions, ownership, timestamps, block pointers - ext4: journaling, extent-based allocation, good general-purpose choice - XFS: scalable to large files, parallel allocations, better for concurrent I/O - Page cache:…
